channel.title: The Scholarly Handover
channel.description: Daily source-grounded academic morning briefing: Paper of the Morning, Knowledge Revisit, Strategic Field Briefing.
channel.itunes:author: The Scholarly Handover

item.title: What would Magnet cost? Pricing the work environment in German hospitals · 19 Aug 2026
item.description: Magnet economics in German hospitals, sensitivity analysis, and the WissZeitVG clears cabinet Paper: The economics of implementing Magnet® designation: relevant parameters for a cost-benefit analysis in the German hospital context (BMC Health Services Research 2026). Revisit: sensitivity analysis. Strategic: German cabinet approves the WissZeitVG reform (29 July 2026): statutory minimum durations for first fixed-term academic contracts and family/care protections extended to third-party-funded posts; Bundestag deliberation from autumn.

item.title: Feeling Rules and Formal Lotteries · 11 Aug 2026
item.description: Hochschild's feeling rules, Acker's gendered organisations, and grants by formal lottery Paper: Emotion Work, Feeling Rules, and Social Structure (American Journal of Sociology 1979). Revisit: Joan Acker (gendered organisations). Strategic: Nature feature (published this morning, 11 August 2026): more than a dozen funders now award grants by partial lottery among fundable proposals; Wellcome and some German programmes are on the list, and the British Academy trial shows diversity gains with no score adjustment.

item.title: The Framework Behind the Frameworks · 31 Jul 2026
item.description: The framework behind the frameworks, what a mechanism actually is, and a new hand on health in Berlin Paper: A new framework for developing and evaluating complex interventions: update of Medical Research Council guidance (BMJ 2021). Revisit: mechanism. Strategic: German cabinet reshuffle, 29 July: Carsten Linnemann becomes Federal Health Minister as Nina Warken moves to head the Chancellery; the PNOG care reform missed the last pre-recess cabinet sitting and now reaches the Bundestag in autumn at the earliest.

item.title: Hypervisible and Unpromoted · 30 Jul 2026
item.description: What a university counts as work, and what a regulator counts as progress Paper: Navigating microaggressions in the workplace: experiences of Chinese international academics in England (Higher Education 2026). Revisit: measurement invariance. Strategic: The NMC's anti-racism principles (published 29 May 2026) put a hard date on UK healthcare providers: a gap-analysis self-assessment completed by end of September 2026, repeated in 2027 to evidence progress, with universities aligning curricula from the 2026/27 academic year and a revised Code in October 2027. It lands alongside register data published yesterday showing 293,778 of 867,935 registrants (33.8%) are Black, Asian or ethnic minority for the first time, while joiners fell 21.4% and leavers rose 5.3%..

item.title: Care under control: dystopian nursing, ontological politics, and the 2027 Horizon window · 26 Jul 2026
item.description: Care under control: dystopian nursing, ontological politics, and the 2027 Horizon window Paper: Nursing as social control: An ethical perspective on care in dystopian contexts (Nursing Ethics (OnlineFirst, 22 July 2026) 2026). Revisit: ontological politics. Strategic: Horizon Europe Cluster 1 (Health) work programme 2026-2027: the 2027 calls (opening February and June 2027) are the live window, and consortium formation starts now; Destinations 4 (health systems) and 5 (digital/AI) are the fits for a nursing workforce and implementation science profile.

item.title: Reassembling the Care Network · 25 Jul 2026
item.description: AI joins the care network, Braidotti's posthuman, and who draws the DFG's infrastructure map Paper: Artificial Intelligence, Cancer Nursing, and Sexual Health: Reassembling Care Networks in Digital Care (Journal of Advanced Nursing 2026). Revisit: Rosi Braidotti (critical posthumanism). Strategic: DFG opens a multi-stage dialogue process on digital research practice and cooperative information infrastructures (IFW 26-49, 15 July 2026): community survey now, second consultation to follow, workshop Q1 2027.

item.title: The checklist, the mechanism, and the missing cabinet slot · 24 Jul 2026
item.description: The checklist, the mechanism, and the missing cabinet slot Paper: Consolidated criteria for reporting qualitative research (COREQ): a 32-item checklist for interviews and focus groups (International Journal for Quality in Health Care 2007). Revisit: realist evaluation. Strategic: Germany's PNOG long-term care reform missed cabinet again on 22 July (fifth postponement since May); Wednesday 29 July is the last cabinet sitting before the summer recess, with entry into force still planned for 1 January 2027.

item.title: Matters of Care: Puig de la Bellacasa, Federici, and a seat at the DFG table · 21 Jul 2026
item.description: Care, three ways: an ethos, a wage, and a ballot Paper: Matters of care in technoscience: Assembling neglected things (Social Studies of Science 2011). Revisit: Silvia Federici. Strategic: DFG Fachkollegienwahl 2027: nominations open now via the new eNominierungs-Plattform; hard deadline 6 November 2026, 14:00. First-ever ballot in which Pflegewissenschaft (Fach 2.22-31) has its own seats..

item.title: Violence as a moral event, the ward inside your standard errors, and nursing science enters the DFG · 20 Jul 2026
item.description: Violence as a moral event, the ward inside your standard errors, and nursing science enters the DFG Paper: "They leave crying": An exploration of moral distress in nurses facing workplace violence (Nursing Ethics 2026). Revisit: clustering and intraclass correlation. Strategic: Pflegewissenschaft appears for the first time in the DFG Fächerstruktur: Fach 2.22-31 (with psychosomatic medicine and general practice, two seats) for the Fachkollegienwahl 2027, term 2028-2032; nomination rights decided summer 2026, election autumn 2027.

item.title: Who Pays for Thinking Time · 19 Jul 2026
item.description: Who pays for thinking time: Spinoza, Marx, and the political economy of free hours Paper: Spinoza and Marx on Free Time and Emendation of the Intellect: Bridging Ethics and Political Economy (Felsefe Arkivi / Archives of Philosophy 2026). Revisit: underdetermination. Strategic: Wissenschaftsrat position paper 'Für Prävention und Gesundheitsförderung' (Drs. 3003-26, Feb 2026) names nursing science a central discipline for prevention-implementation research.

item.title: Description, Outcomes, Delay · 17 Jul 2026
item.description: Sandelowski's quiet classic, eight ways implementation can fail, and the workforce plan stuck in a drawer Paper: Whatever happened to qualitative description? (Research in Nursing & Health 2000). Revisit: implementation outcomes. Strategic: NHS 10-Year Workforce Plan 'largely done' but held back: health secretary gave no publication date at the 8 July committee session, while six unions and royal colleges demand a pause over nurse growth cut from 170,000-190,000 to 50,000 and unevidenced AI productivity assumptions.

item.title: Climate, Coefficient, Contract · 16 Jul 2026
item.description: German diversity climate data, Cronbach's alpha, and the fixed-term contracts reform Paper: Diversity climate and discrimination at German universities: a cross-sectional study among students in health-related degree programs (BMC Medical Education 2026). Revisit: Cronbach's alpha. Strategic: WissZeitVG reform in motion: BMFTR draft bill of 26 May 2026 sets minimum contract durations (3 years pre-doc, 2 years post-doc), extends family and care protections to third-party-funded posts; Bundestag debated 9 July, cabinet expected late summer, parliamentary passage from September.

item.title: Nurse-initiated care at scale, what integration demands, and Germany's slow-fast nursing law · 15 Jul 2026
item.description: Nurse-initiated care at scale, what integration demands, and Germany's slow-fast nursing law Paper: Implementation evaluation of nurse-initiated care in 29 Australian emergency departments: a RE-AIM multi-method evaluation (Implementation Science 2026). Revisit: mixed methods integration. Strategic: Germany's nursing scope-of-practice law (BEEP, ex-Pflegekompetenzgesetz) is in force, but the section 73d SGB V framework contract defining what nurses may actually do is due 31 December 2026, and pay rules not until April 2028; the positioning window for implementation research is now.

item.title: The View from Somewhere · 14 Jul 2026
item.description: The view from somewhere: Haraway's situated knowledges, Annemarie Mol, and who gets into the conference Paper: Situated Knowledges: The Science Question in Feminism and the Privilege of Partial Perspective (Feminist Studies 1988). Revisit: Annemarie Mol. Strategic: Nature Human Behaviour comment (3 July 2026): an audit of 161 conference websites finds substantial gaps in published disability access information; the authors propose quick, low-budget fixes.

item.title: The Package, Not the Personalisation · 13 Jul 2026
item.description: The algorithm picks the therapy, the interaction does the work, and Berlin blinks on care reform Paper: Alleviating Nurse Burnout With an Artificial Intelligence-Selected Mobile Cognitive Behavioral Therapy-Based Intervention: Mixed Methods Randomized Controlled Trial (JMIR mHealth and uHealth 2026). Revisit: interaction effects. Strategic: Germany's Pflegeneuordnungsgesetz (PNOG) stalls before cabinet: long-term care insurance reform draft (RefE 4 June 2026) slips into July amid heavy criticism; remaining cabinet dates 15, 22, 29 July; measures include suspending Tariftreue wage rules until 2029.

item.title: Refusal as Method · 12 Jul 2026
item.description: A manifesto against psychiatry, the ethics of being believed, and the detector arms race Paper: Madpessimism: A Manifesto (Nursing Inquiry 2026). Revisit: epistemic injustice. Strategic: Nature feature (6 July 2026): universities are relying on AI-detection software to catch cheating, and the tools fail worst on second-language writers.

item.title: Normalisation, Consolidated · 08 Jul 2026
item.description: Twenty-five years of NPT in one paper, the detective logic of process tracing, and the UK's standing bet on workforce research Paper: Normalisation Process Theory: Its consolidation and application in implementation research and practice (NIHR Open Research 2026). Revisit: process tracing. Strategic: NIHR's standing cross-programme theme 'Shaping and supporting the health, public health and social care workforce of the future' (DHSC Area of Research Interest 3): researcher-led alignment open at any time, commissioned waves cycling (e.g. discharge-delivery call, outline deadline 14 September 2026).

item.title: Matter that does, institutions that don't: Barad, Ahmed, and a narrowing Wellcome door · 07 Jul 2026
item.description: The performativity of matter, the non-performativity of institutions, and a Wellcome door that half-closes in October Paper: Posthumanist Performativity: Toward an Understanding of How Matter Comes to Matter (Signs: Journal of Women in Culture and Society 2003). Revisit: Sara Ahmed. Strategic: Wellcome Career Development Awards: mid-career leadership funding, with an eligibility change from 29 October 2026 that leaves the UK as the only high-income-country base Wellcome will fund.

item.title: The burnout league table · 06 Jul 2026
item.description: Mindfulness tops the league table; that is the finding, and the problem Paper: Comparative effectiveness of individual-level psychosocial interventions for nurse burnout and its core dimensions: A systematic review and network meta-analysis (International Journal of Nursing Studies (vol 182, art 105622) 2026). Revisit: effect size. Strategic: G-BA Innovationsfonds 2026 Versorgungsforschung calls confirmed published 19 June: guideline projects close 22.09.2026 12:00; themenspezifisch and themenoffen research close 20.10.2026 12:00.

item.title: Reflect, Refract, Persevere · 04 Jul 2026
item.description: AI governance's ethics-washing problem, Spinoza's real ethics, and a deadline that just moved Paper: Beyond ethics washing: evaluating the responsiveness of US, EU, and UN AI governance to expert warnings (AI and Ethics 2026). Revisit: Spinoza. Strategic: EU 'Digital Omnibus on AI' finalised 29 June 2026 (Parliament vote 16 June, 423-57-174): defers the AI Act's high-risk obligations from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027 for stand-alone systems (diagnosis, clinical decision support, triage, monitoring), and to 2 August 2028 for AI embedded in regulated products such as medical devices.

item.title: What Actually Makes Nurses Leave · 22 Jun 2026
item.description: Actual turnover not intention, confidence intervals read properly, and a European policy tailwind for workforce grants Paper: Drivers of frontline registered nurse turnover: evidence from the 2022 National Sample Survey of Registered Nurses (Health Affairs Scholar, 4(6), qxag140 2026). Revisit: Confidence interval. Strategic: European Parliament votes on the EU Health Workforce Own-Initiative (INI) Report; EFN commentary reads it as political backing for safe staffing, advanced practice nursing and workforce sustainability across the EU.

item.title: Process evaluation, fidelity versus adaptation, and a German call that lands today · 19 Jun 2026
item.description: Process evaluation, fidelity versus adaptation, and a German call that lands today Paper: Process evaluation of complex interventions: Medical Research Council guidance (BMJ 2015). Revisit: Fidelity and adaptation. Strategic: G-BA Innovationsfonds Versorgungsforschung 2026 call expected to publish 19 June 2026 (today); submission expected ~October 2026 (provisional).

item.title: What Braun and Clarke actually said · 12 Jun 2026
item.description: The methods paper everyone cites and nobody reads, the theory of making things normal, and a Berlin deadline Paper: Using thematic analysis in psychology (Qualitative Research in Psychology 2006). Revisit: normalisation process theory. Strategic: BMFTR call: clinical studies with high relevance for patient care; four modules including systematic reviews (Module 2) and SWATs (Module 4); applications 1 June to 2 September 2026.

item.title: Identity work, honest adjustment, and a bridge into policy · 11 Jun 2026
item.description: Identity work, honest adjustment, and a bridge into policy Paper: Nurturing an evolving identity through role transition: A hermeneutic phenomenological exploration of the lived experiences of nurse academics working in UK universities (Nurse Education Today (vol 166, art. 107212) 2026). Revisit: Adjusted versus unadjusted estimates. Strategic: UKRI Sector Transition Policy Fellowships 2026 open (9 June); 50 fellowships, close 10 September.
